extracted.intended_audience: advocates, stakeholders, and LeadingAge members preparing public comments on a Department of Education proposed rule
extracted.subtask_short: submitting comments on DOE proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting and submitting public comments to the Department of Education (via regulations.gov), emphasizing evidence, personal impact, consideration of trade-offs, and meeting the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound science and reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting comments, agency reviewers look for sound science and reasoning in the comments they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with logical argumentation and relevant evidence; present clear causal links between the rule and its effects so reviewers can evaluate the merits of your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comments unique and include personal/community impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your comments unique and include how this rule will personally impact you and/or your community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain concrete, specific ways the proposed rule affects you, your organization, or your community to provide context and credibility beyond generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address trade-offs and opposing views
rubrics_metrics.description: Address trade-offs and opposing views in your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge potential downsides or counterarguments and explain why your preferred approach is preferable or how harms can be mitigated; this strengthens persuasiveness and demonstrates balanced analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include qualitative and quantitative data where available
rubrics_metrics.description: Include data on the qualitative and quantitative effects the rule may have, if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical evidence, statistics, case examples, or qualitative accounts to substantiate claims about impacts; cite sources where possible to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Department's specific comment page for the rule; submissions sent by other means (e.g., email to the agency) may not be accepted for the official rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission formats: copy/paste or upload file
rubrics_metrics.description: You can either copy and paste your comments into the provided space or upload a file into the comment web form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the regulations.gov comment page you may paste text directly into the comment box or attach a document file—choose the method that preserves formatting and attachments you need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the comment period and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period varies by rule. For example, comments on the Department of Education proposed rule were due Monday, March 2, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the specific deadline for the rule you are commenting on and submit before that date/time; late comments may not be considered.
